2027-05-19.title: Wednesday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time
readings: O Lord, great peace have they who love your law
Whoever is not against us is for us
2027-05-19.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 7 (Year I). Ordinary Time resumed on the Monday after Pentecost; the Angelus has again taken the place of the Regina Caeli, and the Paschal candle now stands by the baptismal font. Liturgical colour: green. No memorial is assigned to this day in the General Roman Calendar; a Mass of the Holy Spirit, still close to Pentecost, or a votive Mass may be chosen.
2027-05-19.verse: But Jesus said, “Do not stop him; for no one who does a deed of power in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me. Whoever is not against us is for us.”
theo: Ben Sira speaks of Wisdom as a mother and a teacher: “Wisdom teaches her children and gives help to those who seek her. Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early morning are filled with joy.” Wisdom here is far more than cleverness. She is the way God's own mind shapes a human life, and to serve her is to serve God: “Those who serve her minister to the Holy One; the Lord loves those who love her.” Then the reading becomes very honest about how Wisdom educates. She does not hand out her secrets on the first day. “For at first she will walk with them on tortuous paths; she will bring fear and dread upon them, and will torment them by her discipline until she trusts them.” Every good teacher, every good parent, knows this. Trust is built through testing, and only then “she will come straight back to them again and gladden them, and will reveal her secrets to them.” The Christian reads this page with new eyes, for St Paul calls Christ crucified “the power of God and the wisdom of God.” The Wisdom that walks with us on crooked paths has a face and a name. The Psalm sings the fruit of that long schooling: “Great peace have those who love your law; nothing can make them stumble.”

The Gospel is short and sharp. John, the son of Zebedee, the one whom Jesus called a “son of thunder,” brings a report that he expects will please his Master: “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.” Notice the words: not following “us.” John is guarding the borders of the group. Jesus answers with surprising openness: “Do not stop him; for no one who does a deed of power in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me. Whoever is not against us is for us.” The same thing had happened to Moses in the desert, when Eldad and Medad prophesied outside the tent of meeting and Joshua wanted them silenced; Moses answered, “Would that all the Lord's people were prophets.” Jesus does not deny that there is one Church, built on the apostles, and at once he warns against causing the little ones to stumble. But he refuses a jealous spirit that cannot rejoice when good is done in his name by others. The Second Vatican Council teaches that many elements of sanctification and truth are found outside the visible structure of the Catholic Church, gifts that belong to the Church of Christ and impel towards unity (Lumen Gentium 8). Wisdom, after all, teaches her children to recognise her work wherever it appears.
outline: Ask: when someone outside my group does good, am I glad or a little jealous?
To love Wisdom is to love life; Christ is the Wisdom of God.
Wisdom tests before she trusts, then gladdens and reveals.
Jesus refuses a jealous spirit: whoever is not against us is for us.
“Whoever is not against us is for us.”
live: Give the first ten minutes of tomorrow morning to the word of God, before the phone and the news.
Name one good work done by another parish, Church or group, and thank God for it aloud today.
2027-05-19.prayer: God of wisdom, you teach your children by paths we do not always understand, and you gladden those who persevere. Make us lovers of your wisdom, which is Christ your Son. Heal our hearts of the jealousy that wants to keep goodness for ourselves; teach us to rejoice wherever your name is honoured and your works are done, and lead all who believe in Christ into the unity he prayed for. Amen.
altar: In the Eucharist the Wisdom of God becomes food: Christ, “the power of God and the wisdom of God,” gives himself to us under the signs of bread and wine. The one table of the altar is also our deepest prayer for the unity of all who bear his name.

quick: Ben Sira: Wisdom teaches her children; whoever loves her loves life.
Wisdom first walks with us on hard paths and tests us, then gladdens us and reveals her secrets.
John tried to stop a man casting out demons in Jesus' name; Jesus said: do not stop him; whoever is not against us is for us.
2027-05-19.action: Thank God today, by name, for one good work done by people outside your own circle.
2027-05-19.question: Do I guard the borders of my group more carefully than I rejoice in God's work?

family.explain: The disciples saw a man doing good things in Jesus' name, but he was not one of their group, so they told him to stop. Jesus said: do not stop him. If someone does good in my name, he is on our side. God is happy whenever good is done, and we should be happy too.
family.intention: We pray for unity among all Christians, and for all people who help the poor and the sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a family, a school or a group we sometimes speak badly about? Can we find one good thing about them today?”

illus: In the Kerala floods of August 2018, fishermen from the coastal villages of Kollam, Alappuzha and Thiruvananthapuram brought their own boats inland and rescued many thousands of people from flooded homes. Nobody asked the stranded families whether they were Hindu, Muslim or Christian, or which party they voted for; the fishermen simply pulled people into the boats. A parish priest in Chengannur said afterwards: that week I learned that the hand that lifts you out of the water is never on the wrong side.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Wisdom of God, teach us your ways and give us hearts glad at every good done in your name. Amen.
share: Whoever loves her loves life (Sirach 4:12). Do I seek God's wisdom, or only information and advice?
At first she will walk with them on tortuous paths (Sirach 4:17). How has a hard season taught me something I could not learn otherwise?
Whoever is not against us is for us (Mark 9:40). Whom have I been quick to treat as an outsider?
pm.resp: O Lord, great peace have they who love your law.
interc: For the unity of all Christians, that we may grow towards the one Church Christ willed.
For teachers, parents and formators, that they may guide with wisdom and patience.
For all who do good outside the Church, that the Spirit may lead them to the fullness of truth.
For young people facing hard paths in study or work, that they may not give up.
For our group, that jealousy and rivalry may have no place among us.
pm.close: Father, your Son is our wisdom and our peace. Make us glad at every sign of your Kingdom, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira tells us that Wisdom is like a mother who teaches her children. Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early morning are filled with joy (Sirach 4:12). Notice: from early morning. The wise person does not wait until the day is spoiled to look for God.

But Wisdom is not a soft teacher. At first she will walk with them on tortuous paths; she will bring fear and dread upon them (Sirach 4:17). She tests us before she trusts us. Every student who has struggled with mathematics, every apprentice who has spent months only sweeping the workshop, knows this. Then, Ben Sira says, she comes straight back and gladdens us, and reveals her secrets. For us Christians this Wisdom has a face: Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God.

In the Gospel John is proud of himself. We saw a man casting out demons in your name, and we stopped him, because he was not following us. Not following us. How easily we say this too: not our parish, not our association, not our Church. Jesus answers: do not stop him. Whoever is not against us is for us (Mark 9:40).

This does not mean that all ways are the same, or that the Church does not matter. It means that we never become jealous of God's goodness. Wherever the sick are healed, the poor are fed and the name of Jesus is honoured, we rejoice, and we pray that all may come to the fullness of his truth and to the unity he prayed for. Let us ask Wisdom to make our hearts as wide as the heart of Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, once the disciples saw a man doing good things in Jesus' name. But he was not in their group, so they told him to stop! Jesus said: do not stop him. Jesus is happy whenever someone does good. So when another child does something kind, even if they are not your friend, you can be happy too and say: thank you, God!

intro: Theme: “Whoever is not against us is for us.”
Wisdom who teaches her children, the hard paths of her schooling, and a Lord who will not let jealousy shrink his Kingdom.

sub: To love Wisdom is to love life.
q: I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me.
but to those who are the called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
points.apply: Begin each day this week with ten minutes of the Gospel before anything else.

sub: Discipline that hurts for a time.
q: Then she will come straight back to them again and gladden them, and will reveal her secrets to them.
Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
points.apply: Thank God this week for one hard season of your life and the lesson it gave you.

sub: Moses and the two prophets in the camp.
Glad at every good done in his name.
q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!”
Whoever is not against us is for us.
points.apply: Pray by name this week for another parish, Church or group, and speak well of them to someone.

concl: Wisdom schools us patiently, through hard paths, until our hearts can be trusted with her secrets.
A heart formed by Christ's wisdom is never jealous of God's goodness, and prays for the unity of all who bear his name.
2027-05-19.resolve: Each day this week, thank God for one good work done by people outside your own circle.
